questions.question: When a fuel undergoes combustion (burning), what happens to the energy stored within it?
options: It is destroyed completely.
It is transferred to the surroundings by heating.
It is absorbed from the surroundings.
It is converted into chemical potential energy inside the fuel.

questions.question: How can you experimentally compare the amounts of energy transferred by different fuels in a school laboratory?
options: By measuring the volume of gas produced when they are mixed with water
By heating water in a boiling tube and measuring the temperature increase
By measuring the speed at which each fuel evaporates at room temperature
By comparing the mass of the fuels before they are mixed with acids

questions.question: To make a fair comparison of the energy released by different fuels, which variable must be kept constant regarding the fuel itself?
options: The temperature of the fuel before ignition
The mass of the fuel used in each test
The state of matter of the fuel
The color of the fuel

questions.question: In an experiment comparing fuels by heating water in a boiling tube, which of the following must be kept the same for each measurement to ensure a fair test?
options: The starting temperature and volume of the water
The material of the beaker holding the fuel
The size of the room where the experiment is done
The amount of oxygen in the room

questions.question: How can you identify where a substance undergoes a state change when looking at its cooling curve graph?
options: By finding the steepest diagonal drop on the curve
By looking for flat horizontal sections (plateaus) on the curve
By finding the point where the curve starts to rise
By looking at the very end of the curve where it touches the x-axis

questions.question: As a warm liquid cools down without changing state, what physical change is observed and what is happening to its energy?
options: Its temperature decreases as energy is released to the surroundings
Its temperature increases as energy is absorbed from the surroundings
Its temperature remains constant as energy is absorbed from the surroundings
Its temperature decreases as energy is created inside the liquid

questions.question: Which of the following is a key observation that indicates an exothermic chemical reaction is taking place?
options: A decrease in the temperature of the surroundings
An increase in the temperature of the surroundings
The temperature of the surroundings remains exactly the same
The substance changes from a gas to a solid without any temperature change

questions.question: If a chemical reaction is endothermic, what effect will it have on the temperature of its surroundings?
options: The temperature of the surroundings will increase.
The temperature of the surroundings will decrease.
The temperature of the surroundings will fluctuate up and down.
The temperature of the surroundings will remain completely unchanged.

questions.question: During an exothermic chemical reaction, where does the energy transfer occur?
options: From the surroundings to the reactants
From the reactants to the surroundings
From the products to the reactants
From the surroundings to the products

questions.question: In an endothermic reaction, how is energy transferred between the system and its surroundings?
options: Energy is transferred from the surroundings to the products.
Energy is transferred from the reactants to the surroundings.
Energy is destroyed during the chemical process.
Energy is transferred from the products to the surroundings.

questions.question: Why are the physical processes of melting, evaporation, and boiling classified as endothermic?
options: They transfer energy out into the surroundings.
They require energy to be transferred into the substance from the surroundings.
They cause the temperature of the surroundings to rise.
They happen only when a substance releases thermal energy.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of state changes are exothermic processes?
options: Melting and boiling
Evaporating and condensing
Condensing and freezing
Subliming and melting

questions.question: In the UK, over half of the electricity is currently generated using which group of energy sources?
options: Coal, oil, and natural gas
Nuclear power, biomass, and coal
The Sun, wind, and falling water
Geothermal energy, waves, and wood

questions.question: Which of the following fossil fuels is no longer used to generate electricity in UK power stations?
options: Natural gas
Oil
Coal
Biomass

questions.question: Which group of fuels all produce greenhouse gases and pollutants when they are burned?
options: Sun, wind, and falling water
Natural gas, oil, waste, and wood
Hydrogen, helium, and pure oxygen
Uranium, wind, and solar energy

questions.question: What makes an energy resource 'renewable'?
options: It can be burned multiple times without losing its mass.
It is replenished more quickly than we use it up.
It does not release any carbon dioxide when burned.
It is synthetic and made in a laboratory.

questions.question: How do solar panels differ from most other electricity-generating technologies?
options: They require moving steam to spin a turbine.
They produce electricity without using electric generators.
They burn biomass to generate an electric current.
They require falling water to spin magnets.
